units.translation: 22f. The ⟦1⟧, situated high on the ascent to the summit of Parnassus, is described in detail by ⟦2⟧, according to whom this cave was the largest of all known to him; at the end he says: ⟦3⟧. See also ⟦4⟧; ⟦5⟧; ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧, etc. — With the brachylogy ⟦8⟧ . . (the Nymphs who dwell where . .) Weckl. compares 689 ⟦9⟧ (⟦10⟧) ⟦11⟧.
and the people around Parnassus consider it sacred especially to the Corycian Nymphs and to Pan
⟦1⟧ as is natural, since caves are suitable for nesting;

⟦1⟧ (of the Nymphs and of Pan) ⟦2⟧., as ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧ Frg. 243, ⟦7⟧ 264, according to which ⟦8⟧, like the other manuscripts except M, is highly recommended in comparison with the ⟦9⟧ of the scholiast (M ⟦10⟧).

⟦1⟧ = ⟦2⟧. "to stay" already in Homer ⟦3⟧ 326; therefore ⟦4⟧ "place of stay" (wrongly explained by Dindorf as deverticulum). Cf. the grotto in Ithaca ⟦5⟧, which is likewise sacred to the Nymphs. Aristonoos (on 7f. 10) says V. 33 ff.: ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧, ⟦10⟧ etc.
the Nymphs in the Corycian caves

Dionysus (⟦1⟧ as often in the poets, ⟦2⟧ etc.) had great veneration in Delphi (Preller-Robert Mythol. 686); in particular the heights of Parnassus were sacred to him, where he celebrated his dances with his Bacchae by torchlight, ⟦3⟧ etc.; so also ⟦4⟧ of the peaks of P.: ⟦5⟧. Therefore Dionysus also had to be mentioned by the Pythia: ⟦6⟧ ("nor must I forget Bacchus" Paley). The lesser manuscripts have against M ⟦7⟧', which anapest would be somewhat covered by ⟦8⟧ ⟦9⟧ and ⟦10⟧ ⟦11⟧; but some compulsion is always the reason for this foot, and here there was no compulsion.
and the Thyiades rave for Dionysus and Apollo on these occasions

⟦1⟧ like ⟦2⟧ (⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧); ⟦5⟧ like ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧. ⟦8⟧, Kühner-Gerth I 409 f. That Pentheus according to this passage must have been torn to pieces on Parnassus, whereas according to Aeschylus' Xantriai the scene was Cithaeron, is an erroneous assumption of the scholiast. Rather (Weckl.): on his victorious march, after overcoming Pentheus, Dionysus also took Parnassus.
